title: The facade stayed exactly where it was
blurb: Weatherboards repaired, leadlight retained, the picket fence and front garden reinstated. From the footpath the house reads as it always did — which is the point.

title: A new rear pavilion, resolved against the original roof
blurb: The old lean-to came off and a raked-ceiling pavilion went on. High-level glazing along the gable pulls light deep into the plan, and the whole rear wall opens to the garden.

title: One room for cooking, eating and everything else
blurb: Kitchen, dining and living share a single volume under the rake, with the ceiling dropping as it meets the original house so the junction reads deliberately.

title: Fluted island, stone tops and a pantry that hides the mess
blurb: A single stone-topped island with fluted joinery, a window splashback instead of tiles, and a butler’s pantry behind holding the second sink and everything that lives on the bench.

title: Terrazzo, fluted glass and vertical tile
blurb: Main bathroom with a fully glazed bath-shower recess, terrazzo to dado height and vertical stack tile above. The ensuite runs the same palette with a double vanity.

title: Four bedrooms, all with proper storage
blurb: Original front bedrooms kept their leadlight and ceiling height. The new ones got built-in robes, so nothing has to live on a chair.

title: Bluestone, lawn and a level change that works
blurb: Bluestone paving off the living room, a raised lawn behind a low retaining wall, and stepping stones through to the studio at the rear.
